simple.meaning: רִיק (rîyq) is a Hebrew word meaning “emptiness ; figuratively, a worthless thing; adverbially, in vain.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: רִיק (H7385) appears 12 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Leviticus 26:16, with occurrences in Leviticus, Job, Psalms, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and 1 more.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רִיק (H7385) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in רִיק (H7385) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: רִיק (rîyq) / H7385 is traced through Leviticus 26:16, Leviticus 26:20, Job 39:16, Psalms 2:1 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

timeline.evidenceText: I also will do this to you: I will appoint terror over you, even consumption and fever, that shall consume the eyes, and make the soul to pine away. You will sow your seed in vain, for your enemies will eat it.
Your strength will be spent in vain; for your land won’t yield its increase, neither will the trees of the land yield their fruit.
She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers.
But know that Yahweh has set apart for himself him who is godly:
Surely I have cleansed my heart in vain,
For Egypt helps in vain, and to no purpose; therefore I have called her Rahab who sits still.
But I said, “I have labored in vain.
They will not labor in vain
“Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon has devoured me.
Behold, isn’t it of Yahweh of Armies that the peoples labor for the fire, and the nations weary themselves for vanity?

definitions.short: emptiness ; figuratively, a worthless thing; adverbially, in vain
definitions.usage: empty, to no purpose, (in) vain (thing), vanity.
definitions.full: H7385. riyq רִיק noun [masculine] emptiness, vanity ; — chiefly in adverb phrase לְרִיק Isa 46:4 ; Job 39:16 in vain (of labour without benefit), so ׳לָר Lev 26:16 , 20 (H), Isa 65:23 ; and as adverb accusative רִיק 30:7 ; Psa 73:13 , probably also 2:1 (most = empty scheme as רֵיק 2 ) compare 4:3 (read probably רֵיק ); דִיק בְּדֵי Jer 51:58 = Hab 2:13 . — Jer 51:34 see רֵיק 1 above
